body: New York's Appellate Division, Second Department ruled on October 21, 2026 that sublessor VK Dental Group, Inc. was not entitled to summary judgment on its claims for unpaid sublease rent, reversing a Supreme Court, Kings County judgment of $1,004,426.20 against Tender Touch Physical Therapy, PLLC and the other sublessees. The decision and order was issued by a four-justice panel.

According to the decision, in January 2017 Metrotech Smile Dental, P.C. leased property from 350 Fulton Realty, LLC, which is not a party. In March 2017 Metrotech subleased the premises to the defendants, and in April 2018 it assigned its lease to VK Dental, which became the sublessor.

VK Dental sued in May 2022, alleging the sublessees failed to pay rent and that it was forced to surrender possession of the premises. After a hearing at which a VK Dental witness testified, the trial court granted summary judgment in an order dated October 21, 2024, and entered judgment on November 21, 2024.

The Second Department held that, even setting aside the hearing testimony, VK Dental showed the sublessees had not paid rent for certain months. But the sublessees' principal stated in an affidavit that VK Dental failed to pay 50% of utilities as the subleases required and had the gas service disconnected. Because a breach-of-contract plaintiff must prove its own performance, that raised a triable issue of fact. The court reversed the judgment, denied the summary judgment motion, dismissed the separate appeal from the order because it merged into the judgment, and awarded the sublessees one bill of costs.
